system.one_liner: Linear probes on layer-wise hidden states test how well vision-only, vision-language and multimodal models encode latitude and longitude.

content.variant_note: a residual-stream row of layers from input image to output caption, with one tap per layer dropping into a separate linear-probe box (activation vector, ridge regression, predicted-versus-true plot)
content.argues: Whether a model encodes geolocation can be tested by fitting a ridge-regression probe on each layer's [CLS] or last-token residual and scoring latitude/longitude predictions with R².
content.subject: An image through a residual layer stack whose per-layer activations feed a ridge-regression probe of latitude and longitude.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw an analysis setup as the model's own residual-stream row with one tap per layer dropping into a separate tinted probe box, then spell the probe out in three beats (vector, regressor, predicted-versus-true plot with its score) plus its formula.

evidence: Schematic illustration of our linear probing analysis setup.
We fit ridge regression models W on the [CLS] or last token residuals A(l) from each layer l

summary: The paper analyses how well vision-only models (ViT), vision-language models (CLIP) and multimodal foundation models (LLaVA, Qwen, Gemma) encode geolocation, and finds that textual supervision helps. Figure 1 is a schematic of the linear-probing setup. An input image (a stack of photos, the front one the Step Pyramid of Djoser) enters a blue-tinted model drawn as a row of layers joined by residual circled-plus nodes, marked by a robot icon, and the model outputs a caption naming the pyramid and Saqqara in orange. From each layer a tap A(1) to A(L) drops into a pink Linear Probing box: an activation vector goes into a Ridge Regression box, giving a predicted-versus-true lat/lon scatter with R² = 0.75, with the ridge objective written below.
summary_zh: 论文分析视觉模型、视觉语言模型与多模态大模型对地理位置的编码，发现文本监督有帮助。图为线性探测的示意：输入图片经带残差的多层模型，每层激活 A(l) 向下接入粉色探测框，岭回归预测经纬度并以 R²=0.75 的散点示意。
notes: The prior attribute panels=2 was not followed: the blue model band and the pink probe box are tinted containers in one drawing, not framed panels. The scatter is vector (the five bitmaps are four photos and the robot); R² = 0.75 is printed on it but the dots look schematic. The text layer splits Layer into L + ayer and holds one text item per scatter dot; none of that shows in the print.
